report.sampleFormatNote: Valid Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS CSV traffic logs with standard field ordering including subtype, timestamps, IPs, ports, zones, interfaces, bytes, packets, and session metadata.

findings.issue: Field contains the firewall action (allow/drop/deny) instead of the network transport protocol (udp/tcp). The protocol is in field index 29 of the CSV. OCSF connection_info.protocol_name should be 'udp' or 'tcp'.
findings.example: Event 1: protocol_name='allow' but source has 'udp'; Event 2: protocol_name='drop' but source has 'tcp'

findings.issue: activity_id is hardcoded to 1 (Open) for all events regardless of action. OCSF 4001 activity_ids: 1=Open, 2=Close, 3=Reset, 4=Fail, 6=Traffic. Blocked/denied traffic should map to 4 (Fail) or 6, allowed end-session should map to 2 (Close). The action (allow/drop/deny) and subtype (end/drop/deny) are both present and must drive this.
findings.example: Event 2 (drop/policy-deny) has activity_id=1; Event 3 (end/allow) has activity_id=1

findings.issue: type_uid is hardcoded to 400101 for all events. type_uid = class_uid * 100 + activity_id, so it must vary with activity_id. A close event should be 400102, a fail/block should be 400104, etc.
findings.example: All 8 events show type_uid=400101 regardless of action

findings.issue: Destination port is wrong or zeroed for many events. The source CSV has destination port in field index 23 (column 24). For event 1 dst port should be 53, event 2 should be 445, event 4 should be 1433, event 8 should be 22. Instead the pipeline appears to have swapped src/dst ports or misidentified columns.
findings.example: Event 1: dst_endpoint.port=0 but source dst_port=53; Event 4: dst_endpoint.port=0 but source dst_port=1433; Event 8: dst_endpoint.port=0 but source dst_port=22

findings.issue: Source port is mapped to what appears to be the destination port. Event 1 src port should be 54321 (ephemeral), not 53. The pipeline seems to have swapped source and destination ports.
findings.example: Event 1: src_endpoint.port=53 but source src_port=54321; Event 2: src_endpoint.port=445 but source src_port=44512

findings.issue: Bytes fields are mis-mapped. OCSF bytes_in/bytes_out should be total bytes received and sent. The source CSV has total_bytes at index 30, bytes_sent at 31, bytes_received at 32, packets at 33. The pipeline maps packet count to bytes_in and bytes_received to bytes_out instead of the correct byte fields.
findings.example: Event 1: bytes_in=1 (is packet count), bytes_out=64 (is bytes_received); should be bytes_in=64 bytes_received, bytes_out=64 bytes_sent

findings.issue: OCSF Network Activity traffic object supports packets_in and packets_out. The source CSV contains packets_received and packets_sent fields which are present in the input but entirely unmapped.
findings.example: Event 3 source has pkts_sent=35, pkts_received=3; these are absent from output

findings.issue: OCSF Network Activity requires disposition_id to reflect whether traffic was allowed or blocked. This critical field is completely absent. Source action field (allow/drop/deny) must map to disposition_id (1=Allowed, 2=Blocked, etc.).
findings.example: Event 2 action=drop → should be disposition_id=2 (Blocked); Event 1 action=allow → disposition_id=1 (Allowed); all disposition fields missing

findings.issue: The policy/rule name is present in the source (field index 11: Allow-DNS-Out, Default-Deny, Allow-Web-Out, etc.) but is completely unmapped to OCSF firewall_rule.name.
findings.example: Event 1 rule='Allow-DNS-Out'; Event 2 rule='Default-Deny'; all absent from output

findings.issue: Source and destination security zones are present in the source (fields: trust/untrust/dmz) but not mapped to OCSF src_endpoint.zone and dst_endpoint.zone.
findings.example: Event 1: from_zone='trust', to_zone='untrust'; Event 4: from_zone='trust', to_zone='dmz'; all absent

findings.issue: NAT translated source IP (field index 8) and translated destination IP (field index 9) are present in the source but entirely unmapped.
findings.example: Event 3: nat_src='203.0.113.1', nat_dst='172.217.14.100'; absent from output

findings.issue: Session ID is present in source (field index 43: 123456789...) but not mapped to OCSF connection_info.session_id or equivalent.
findings.example: Event 1 session_id=123456789; Event 2 session_id=123456790; all absent

findings.issue: OCSF supports start_time and end_time. The PAN-OS log contains both session start time (field index 6) and log receive time (field index 1). These are present but not mapped.
findings.example: Event 3: session_start='2026/06/25 00:30:12', log_time='2026/06/25 00:31:55'; both absent from output

findings.issue: Session elapsed time (field index 46: e.g., 103, 600, 4) is present in the source but not mapped to OCSF duration or equivalent field.
findings.example: Event 3: elapsed=103; Event 6: elapsed=600; all absent

findings.issue: Session end reason (aged-out, tcp-fin, policy-deny) is present in the source and maps to OCSF connection_info.boundary or a session end reason field, but is entirely absent from output.
findings.example: Event 1: session_end_reason='aged-out'; Event 3: session_end_reason='tcp-fin'; all absent

findings.issue: Application name is present in source (field index 13: dns, ssl, ms-sql-db, youtube, ms-office365) but not mapped to any OCSF field such as app_name or connection_info.protocol_ver.
findings.example: Event 1: app='dns'; Event 3: app='ssl'; Event 5: app='youtube'; all absent

findings.issue: Device model/serial (PA-3220, serial 001234567890) and virtual system (vsys1) are present in source but device object is empty in all output events.
findings.example: device={} in all events; source has serial=001234567890, device_name=PA-3220

findings.issue: Ingress and egress interface names (ethernet1/1, ethernet1/3, ethernet1/2) are present in source but not mapped to OCSF endpoint interface fields.
findings.example: Event 1: inbound_if='ethernet1/1', outbound_if='ethernet1/3'; absent

findings.issue: severity_id is hardcoded to 1 (Informational) for all events including drops and denies. While traffic logs don't carry an explicit severity, blocked/denied actions could reasonably warrant a different severity_id and this should be configurable rather than hardcoded the same for all.
findings.example: Event 2 (drop) and Event 5 (deny) both have severity_id=1

findings.issue: OCSF metadata.log_name and metadata.logged_time (log receipt time) are mappable from the source but absent.
findings.example: metadata contains only product and version; log_name='TRAFFIC' and logged_time from field index 1 absent

findings.issue: When the username field in source is 'unknown', this is not a real user but a PAN-OS placeholder. It is mapped literally as actor.user.name='unknown' which may cause false attribution.
findings.example: Event 2: actor.user.name='unknown' from source field 'unknown'

missingFields: end_time (log receive time / session end time fields present)
app / application name (app field index 13 is present)
nat_src_ip / nat_dst_ip (translated IP fields are present)
report.summary: The pipeline produces structurally valid OCSF Network Activity (4001) events but with severe mapping errors throughout. The most critical failures are: (1) connection_info.protocol_name is set to the firewall action (allow/drop/deny) instead of the transport protocol (tcp/udp); (2) source and destination ports are swapped; (3) bytes_in/bytes_out are mapped to packet counts and wrong byte columns; (4) activity_id and type_uid are hardcoded to 1/400101 for all events ignoring the actual action; and (5) the majority of available source fields — disposition, rule name, zones, session ID, app name, NAT IPs, end reason, duration, packets, and device details — are completely absent from the output. Of roughly 25 distinct values the source provides, fewer than 7 are correctly mapped.
lessons: For PAN-OS CSV traffic logs, carefully index all columns: the transport protocol (tcp/udp) is at index 29, source port at index 24, destination port at index 23, bytes_sent at index 31, bytes_received at index 32, packets_sent at index 35, packets_received at index 34 — do not confuse action (index 30) with protocol, and do not confuse packet count (index 33) with bytes.

OCSF activity_id for Network Activity (4001) MUST be derived from the firewall action and session subtype: allow+end→2 (Close), drop or deny→4 (Fail); type_uid must always equal class_uid*100+activity_id and never be hardcoded.
disposition_id is a mandatory OCSF field for firewall traffic events — always map the firewall action (allow=1 Allowed, drop/deny=2 Blocked) to this field; omitting it makes the event non-conformant.
Never leave the device{} object empty when the source provides serial number and model (PA-3220, 001234567890); map these to device.uid and device.name respectively.

Map all contextually rich fields the source provides: firewall_rule.name from policy name, src/dst endpoint zones, session_id, app name, NAT translated IPs, session end reason, elapsed duration, and interface names — these are all present in PAN-OS traffic logs and have clear OCSF target fields.
